lines.text: Two lines cross inside a triangle, and one piece is shaded.
lines.caption: Two lines cross inside a triangle, and one piece is shaded.

lines.text: It's tempting to guess half the triangle. <short pause> But the real answer is sneakier.
lines.caption: It's tempting to guess half the triangle. But the real answer is sneakier.

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's crack it together.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's crack it together.

lines.text: Here's the question. Triangle A B C has area sixty.
lines.caption: Here's the question. Triangle A B C has area sixty.

lines.text: D is the midpoint of B C.
lines.caption: D is the midpoint of B C.

lines.text: E is on A C, and A E to E C is two to one.
lines.caption: E is on A C, and A E to E C is two to one.

lines.text: Segments A D and B E meet at point P. What is the area of the shaded triangle A B P?
lines.caption: Segments A D and B E meet at point P. What is the area of the shaded triangle A B P?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: So what do we really know?
lines.caption: So what do we really know?

lines.text: D cuts B C into two equal halves. E cuts A C into three equal parts: two near A, one near C.
lines.caption: D cuts B C into two equal halves. E cuts A C into three equal parts: two near A, one near C.

lines.text: The real puzzle is where P sits on A D. Once we know that, we're nearly done.
lines.caption: The real puzzle is where P sits on A D. Once we know that, we're nearly done.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's start with one handy rule.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's start with one handy rule.

lines.text: Two triangles with the same corner, and bases on the same line, have the same height.
lines.caption: Two triangles with the same corner, and bases on the same line, have the same height.

lines.text: So their areas compare just like their bases.
lines.caption: So their areas compare just like their bases.

lines.text: D is the midpoint, so triangles A B D and A D C each get half of sixty. That's thirty each.
lines.caption: D is the midpoint, so triangles A B D and A D C each get half of sixty. That's thirty each.

lines.text: Now draw one more line, from C to P. That cuts the triangle into five pieces.
lines.caption: Now draw one more line, from C to P. That cuts the triangle into five pieces.

lines.text: Look at B P D and C P D. Same corner P, equal bases. So they're equal. Call each one x.
lines.caption: Look at B P D and C P D. Same corner P, equal bases. So they're equal. Call each one x.

lines.text: Now A P E and C P E. Same corner P, and A E is double the length of E C.
lines.caption: Now A P E and C P E. Same corner P, and A E is double the length of E C.

lines.text: So A P E is twice as big. Call C P E y, and A P E two y.
lines.caption: So A P E is twice as big. Call C P E y, and A P E two y.

lines.text: Time for two equations. Triangle A D C is thirty, and its pieces are x, y and two y.
lines.caption: Time for two equations. Triangle A D C is thirty, and its pieces are x, y and two y.

lines.text: So x plus three y equals thirty.
lines.caption: So x plus three y equals thirty.

lines.text: Next, triangle B E C. It shares corner B with the big triangle, and E C is one third of A C.
lines.caption: Next, triangle B E C. It shares corner B with the big triangle, and E C is one third of A C.

lines.text: So B E C is one third of sixty, which is twenty. Its pieces are x, x and y.
lines.caption: So B E C is one third of sixty, which is twenty. Its pieces are x, x and y.

lines.text: So two x plus y equals twenty.
lines.caption: So two x plus y equals twenty.

lines.text: Let's double the first equation. Two x plus six y equals sixty.
lines.caption: Let's double the first equation. Two x plus six y equals sixty.

lines.text: The other one says two x plus y equals twenty. The difference is five y, and that's forty.
lines.caption: The other one says two x plus y equals twenty. The difference is five y, and that's forty.

lines.text: So y is eight. Then two x plus eight is twenty, so x is six.
lines.caption: So y is eight. Then two x plus eight is twenty, so x is six.

lines.text: A B D is thirty, and B P D is six. So A B P is thirty minus six: <short pause> twenty-four! That's C.
lines.caption: A B D is thirty, and B P D is six. So A B P is thirty minus six: twenty-four! That's C.

lines.text: Check: A B P and A P E make A B E. Twenty-four plus sixteen is forty, two thirds of sixty.
lines.caption: Check: A B P and A P E make A B E. Twenty-four plus sixteen is forty, two thirds of sixty.

lines.text: Here's a second way, with one clever extra line.
lines.caption: Here's a second way, with one clever extra line.

lines.text: Here's the rule we need. A line parallel to one side of a triangle cuts the other two sides in the same ratio.
lines.caption: Here's the rule we need. A line parallel to one side of a triangle cuts the other two sides in the same ratio.

lines.text: From D, draw a line parallel to B E. It meets A C at a new point, F.
lines.caption: From D, draw a line parallel to B E. It meets A C at a new point, F.

lines.text: D is halfway along C B. So the parallel line lands halfway along C E. F is the midpoint of E C.
lines.caption: D is halfway along C B. So the parallel line lands halfway along C E. F is the midpoint of E C.

lines.text: Now count steps along A C. E C is two steps, so A E is four steps, and E F is one.
lines.caption: Now count steps along A C. E C is two steps, so A E is four steps, and E F is one.

lines.text: In triangle A D F, P E is parallel to D F. So A P to P D matches A E to E F: four to one.
lines.caption: In triangle A D F, P E is parallel to D F. So A P to P D matches A E to E F: four to one.

lines.text: So A P is four fifths of A D. That makes A B P four fifths of A B D.
lines.caption: So A P is four fifths of A D. That makes A B P four fifths of A B D.

lines.text: Four fifths of thirty is twenty-four. Same answer! It's C.
lines.caption: Four fifths of thirty is twenty-four. Same answer! It's C.

lines.text: When would you pick this way? When you need a ratio along a line, fast, with no equations.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? When you need a ratio along a line, fast, with no equations.

lines.text: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Thirty is triangle A B D, half the whole. Too big, because A B P is only part of it.
lines.caption: Thirty is triangle A B D, half the whole. Too big, because A B P is only part of it.

lines.text: Forty is triangle A B E, two thirds of the whole. Also too big.
lines.caption: Forty is triangle A B E, two thirds of the whole. Also too big.

lines.text: Twenty is what you'd get if you copied two to one onto A D. Two thirds of thirty is twenty.
lines.caption: Twenty is what you'd get if you copied two to one onto A D. Two thirds of thirty is twenty.

lines.text: But two to one belongs to line A C. Line A D has its own split: four to one.
lines.caption: But two to one belongs to line A C. Line A D has its own split: four to one.

lines.text: Fifteen is what you'd get if P were the midpoint of A D. Half of thirty is fifteen.
lines.caption: Fifteen is what you'd get if P were the midpoint of A D. Half of thirty is fifteen.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. Every line gets its own ratio. Find it before you use it.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. Every line gets its own ratio. Find it before you use it.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Here's a new triangle with area eighty-four.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Here's a new triangle with area eighty-four.

lines.text: D is still the midpoint of B C. But now A E to E C is three to one.
lines.caption: D is still the midpoint of B C. But now A E to E C is three to one.

lines.text: What is the area of triangle A B P?
lines.caption: What is the area of triangle A B P?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's use the parallel line. D F is parallel to B E, so F is still the midpoint of E C.
lines.caption: Let's use the parallel line. D F is parallel to B E, so F is still the midpoint of E C.

lines.text: E C is two steps, so A E is six steps, and E F is one. So A P is six sevenths of A D.
lines.caption: E C is two steps, so A E is six steps, and E F is one. So A P is six sevenths of A D.

lines.text: Triangle A B D is half of eighty-four, which is forty-two.
lines.caption: Triangle A B D is half of eighty-four, which is forty-two.

lines.text: Six sevenths of forty-two is thirty-six!
lines.caption: Six sevenths of forty-two is thirty-six!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: When two lines cross inside a triangle, find how the crossing point splits each line.
lines.caption: When two lines cross inside a triangle, find how the crossing point splits each line.

lines.text: Use same-height triangles, or a parallel line. Then take that fraction of a bigger triangle.
lines.caption: Use same-height triangles, or a parallel line. Then take that fraction of a bigger triangle.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
